info.title: HR Platform API
info.description: Internal HR management platform — auth, employees, leaves, standups, projects, servers, payroll, profile, reports, and integrations (Google Calendar, Discord, generic webhooks).

tags.name: Goals
tags.description: Individual, team, and company goals / KPI tracking

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Peer, manager, and public recognition feedback notes

tags.name: Google Calendar
tags.description: Google OAuth connection and calendar sync

tags.name: Meetings
tags.description: Scheduled meetings backed by Google Calendar

tags.name: Discord
tags.description: Discord bot / Webhook Events integration for standups

bearerAuth.description: Obtained from POST /api/auth/login. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

status.description: Create only — 'onboarding' creates a pending applicant (is_active = false) awaiting approval via PUT /{id}/approve or PUT /{id}/reject.

discord_username.description: Update only — matched against Discord standup submissions

ip_address.description: Masked as •••••••• when is_sensitive=true and show_sensitive is not requested

ssh_user.description: Masked as •••••••• when is_sensitive=true and show_sensitive is not requested

email.description: Must be on an allowed organization domain

current_password.description: Required if the account already has a password set

token.description: Token from the reset-password email link

effective_rate.description: Estimated effective tax rate as a percentage

smtp_pass.description: Required on initial setup; omit to keep the stored password unchanged

password.description: Left unchanged if omitted/blank on update

nda_path.description: Stored filename of the uploaded signed contract

get.description: This endpoint provides a quick way to verify if the server is up and running. It returns a JSON object containing the status of the server and the current timestamp.

post.description: This API endpoint allows users to log in using their company email and password. It returns a JWT valid for 7 days and is restricted to email domains of allowed organizations.

put.description: This endpoint allows users to change their password if they are already logged in. The request body should include the new password details.

post.description: Sends a generic message indicating your request has been received, regardless of the email's existence to avoid enumeration.
Use this endpoint to reset your password by providing a valid password reset token. Ensure you include a new password in the request body for the operation to succeed.

get.description: This endpoint provides aggregated data including headcount, leave, and project statistics. It is secured with bearer authentication.
This endpoint returns an array of daily counts for standup submissions over the last 30 days. It can be used by frontend engineers to fetch and display the submission trend on a dashboard.

This endpoint provides an array of daily counts for leave request submissions over the last 30 days. It can be used by frontend engineers to fetch and display the leave submission trend data on a dashboard.
Use this endpoint to retrieve a list of all active employees. The response is an array of employee objects, each following the schema defined for Employee.

post.description: Use this endpoint to create a new employee record. It also automatically seeds default leave balances for the current year.

get.description: Returns an array of employees who are created with is_active set to false, indicating they are awaiting approval. This endpoint is only accessible to users with administrative privileges.
Use this endpoint to retrieve details of an employee by their unique ID. Specify the employee's ID in the URL to fetch their information.

put.description: This endpoint allows updating the details of an employee identified by their unique ID. It requires the employee's ID in the URL and a JSON body with the new employee details to be sent.

delete.description: This endpoint allows you to deactivate an employee by setting their `is_active` to false. It takes an integer `id` as a path parameter to identify the employee to be deactivated.

get.description: This endpoint provides a payroll summary for a specific employee, including details like working days, approved leave days, and expected pay. It's useful for frontend engineers looking to fetch and display payroll information for their applications.

put.description: Approve a pending employee application by setting is_active to true and status to 'active'. Requires admin privileges and sends an email with a one-time password to the employee's company email. Fails if the employee is not in the 'onboarding' status.

400.description: Employee is not a pending applicant

put.description: Permanently deletes an employee record if they are in 'onboarding' status. Requires admin permissions and an employee ID. Sends a rejection notice via email if the 'send_mail' parameter is true.

parameters.name: send_mail
parameters.description: If true, sends a rejection notice to the employee before deleting their record.

400.description: Employee is not a pending applicant

get.description: Retrieve a list of leave requests for a specific employee or filter by request status.

to.description: If provided, sends a notification email via the employee's configured SMTP settings

post.description: This endpoint allows submitting a leave request for an employee. It requires JSON data with employee_id, leave_type, start_date, and end_date, along with optional reason, notification email, and carbon copy/bcc fields.

put.description: Modify a pending leave request by the employee who initiated it. Ensure the status is still "pending" to avoid unauthorized edits.

delete.description: Endorses the cancellation of a pending leave request by the user with the specified ID. Ensure the user is the owner and the status is still 'pending' to proceed.

get.summary: Get employees on approved leave today
get.description: Use this endpoint to retrieve an array of objects containing employee details such as name, designation, profile picture (optional), leave type, and end date who are on approved leave today.

200.description: Array of employees out this week

get.description: This endpoint returns an array of objects containing employee details such as name, designation, leave type, and the dates they are on leave. It's useful for frontend engineers to fetch and display leave information in real-time.
You can use this endpoint to fetch the current year's leave balances for a specific employee. Simply provide the employee's ID in the path parameter to retrieve the data.

put.description: This API endpoint allows administrators or leads to approve a leave request by providing the leave ID and the approver's ID. It ensures the request is only processed by those with appropriate permissions and that the leave dates have not passed.
Rejects a leave request by the specified ID. Requires the admin or lead to be authorized and the request to be within the allowed rejection window.

get.summary: List standups by date or employee_id
get.description: This endpoint allows fetching a list of standups for a specific date or by an employee's ID. Employees can see their own standups, while admins/leads can view all standups and filter by employee ID.

post.description: This endpoint allows users to submit daily standup updates. The request includes the employee's ID, the previous day's and current day's status, any blockers, and the standup date. The system creates a new standup entry or updates an existing one, and if configured, mirrors the standup to Discord.

get.description: This endpoint provides a list of standups submitted by the user today. Access is restricted to authenticated users unless the user is an administrator or lead, in which case they can view all standups.

This endpoint allows you to retrieve an array of projects that an employee (identified by empId) is assigned to, including their roles and milestones. It requires the empId parameter in the path to be provided, and returns the projects in JSON format.
This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of projects, filtering by their status (active, archived, on_hold).

post.description: Use this endpoint to create a new project by providing a project name, description, repository URL(s), documentation URL(s), status, and dates. The response includes the newly created project details.

put.description: Use this endpoint to modify an existing project by providing updated project details in the request body. The project ID is specified in the URL path.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves a list of team assignments for a specific project identified by its ID. It requires the project ID in the path parameter, which should be an integer.

post.description: Assigns an employee to a project with a specified role (lead, backend, frontend, ui_ux, qa, devops). This API allows updating the role of an existing employee assignment.

delete.description: This endpoint allows a frontend engineer to remove an employee's assignment from a specific project by specifying the project ID and employee ID in the request path.

get.description: This endpoint allows you to fetch a list of milestones associated with a specific project identified by its ID. You need to provide the project ID in the URL path to retrieve the milestones.

post.description: This endpoint allows adding a new milestone to a specific project identified by the provided ID. The request should include the milestone's title, due date, and status, with valid status options being 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'.

put.description: Modify the details of a specific project milestone by providing its ID and updating fields like title, due date, and status. Ensure all provided fields are valid and of the correct type to avoid errors.

get.description: This endpoint lists all service keys associated with a specific project identified by the provided ID. It is useful for frontend engineers to retrieve and display service information for further user interactions or backend integrations.

post.description: This endpoint links a project to a specified service by providing the service_key. It is idempotent and returns a success message upon successful linking.

delete.description: Unlinks a specified service from a project identified by the provided ID and service key. Useful for maintaining project dependencies and resource management.

get.description: This endpoint lists servers within a specified project. You can filter the results by setting the `project_id` query parameter. Additionally, you can toggle the visibility of sensitive fields using the `show_sensitive` parameter (requires admin or lead role).

post.description: Use this endpoint to register a new server with details such as name, environment, IP address, and notes. Ensure to provide the necessary parameters in the request body as specified for a successful creation.

put.description: This API endpoint allows updating the details of a server identified by its ID. It requires providing a server object in the request body in JSON format.

delete.description: This API endpoint allows deleting a server record by providing the server's ID in the URL. It is suitable for developers who need to remove server entries from their application's database.

get.description: This endpoint returns an array of the latest culture events. A frontend engineer can integrate this by sending a GET request to /api/events and handling the JSON response containing an array of CultureEvent objects.

post.description: Use this endpoint to create a new culture event. Include the event's title, type (e.g., birthday, anniversary), date, and an optional description to add context.

get.description: This endpoint provides an array of upcoming events that are happening within the next 30 days. It's useful for frontend engineers looking to display live event schedules on their applications.
Retrieve a list of payroll records for active employees. Admins/leads can view all records, others only their own.

put.description: Updates an employee's salary and pay frequency. Requires admin permissions and valid salary update input in JSON format.
Admins can reset a specific employee's password via this endpoint. The request should include a password reset input in JSON format and specify the employee's unique ID in the path.

get.description: Returns an array of tax records for employees, useful for payroll management. Users can filter based on their role to see only their own records.

put.description: This endpoint allows admins to update or create an employee's tax profile. It requires the employee's ID and a JSON payload for the tax profile details. Admins must authenticate with Bearer Auth to use this endpoint.

get.description: Retrieve a list of goals for a specific employee or filter by status and category. Admins/leads can filter by employee_id for comprehensive view.

post.description: Use this API to create a personal goal. Ensure your request includes valid goal details and is made with the correct permissions.

get.description: This endpoint provides an array of summaries, each containing goal completion statistics for a specific employee. It requires bearer authentication for authorization.

put.description: This endpoint allows updating the details of a specific goal. It requires the goal's ID and valid JSON data for the goal's input. Ensure you have the necessary permissions to update the goal.

delete.description: This API allows the deletion of a specific goal identified by its ID. It requires the caller to be authenticated and have the appropriate permissions.

put.description: Use this endpoint to update the progress and status of a specific goal. Provide the goal ID and the new progress value in the request body.

get.description: This endpoint allows fetching performance reviews for a specific employee or filtering by review status. It supports querying by employee ID and review status.

post.description: Creates a draft performance review for an employee. Requires admin or lead permissions and a unique review period per employee.

400.description: A review for this period already exists

get.summary: Get employee rating history by ID
get.description: This endpoint allows you to retrieve the rating history of an employee identified by their ID. It's useful for developers who need to fetch and display an employee's performance trends over time.

put.description: Use this endpoint to update a performance review draft. Ensure the review's status is 'draft' and authenticate with a valid token to make changes.

400.description: Only draft reviews can be edited

delete.description: Deletes a draft review. Ensure the review status is 'draft' and you have the appropriate permissions to delete it.

400.description: Only draft reviews can be deleted

put.description: Used to submit a draft review for an employee. Requires admin or lead permissions and should be called only once per review draft.
Acknowledge a submitted review by the reviewed employee to mark it as acknowledged. Ensure the review's status is 'submitted' for acknowledgment.

400.description: Only submitted reviews can be acknowledged

get.summary: List feedback notes by scope and type
get.description: This endpoint allows retrieval of feedback notes based on the specified scope (public, received, sent) and type (praise, constructive, peer, manager).

400.description: Missing message or sending feedback to yourself

post.description: Use this endpoint to send a feedback note to another employee, ensuring the message is valid and not directed at oneself.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves an array of per-employee summaries of feedback received counts, useful for visualizing feedback distribution across employees.

delete.description: This API endpoint allows authorized users to delete a specific feedback note identified by its ID. It requires a valid ID in the path parameter and appropriate permissions to proceed.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the profile information of the currently logged-in employee. It requires a valid authentication token for authorization.

put.description: This endpoint allows updating the editable fields of a user's profile. It ensures that setting a date of birth also creates a birthday cultural event for the user.

post.description: Use this endpoint to upload or replace your profile photo. It accepts JPEG, PNG, and WEBP files up to 5 MB in size. The previous photo will be deleted.

This API allows users to upload a document image (front or back) related to their citizenship. It supports multipart/form-data for file upload and accepts .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp file types up to 5MB. The endpoint requires a 'side' parameter specifying whether to upload the front or back of the document, and deletes the previous file if an upload with the same 'side' is provided.

400.description: Invalid side or no file uploaded

get.description: Retrieve a list of monthly reports for a specified month and year, suitable for API consumers unfamiliar with the API structure.

post.description: Use this API to submit a monthly report file. The API requires a multipart form containing the report file, employee ID, report title, month, and year. Ensure all required fields are provided, including the report file, otherwise, you may receive a 400 error.

400.description: Missing required fields or no file

get.description: This endpoint allows users to download their own report files by providing the report ID in the URL. The response will be a binary stream of the file.

delete.description: This API allows non-privileged users to delete their own reports. It also ensures that the report file is removed from the disk. The API expects the report's ID to be provided in the path.

get.description: This endpoint returns the OAuth consent URL for Google Calendar, useful for setting up OAuth consent screens. Requires admin privileges and returns a JSON object with the URL.

get.summary: Exchange auth code for tokens and redirect to frontend calendar page
get.description: This endpoint exchanges an auth code provided by Google in the query parameters for access tokens. After receiving the tokens, it redirects the frontend to the calendar page. Developers should use the code provided by Google to authenticate and integrate this endpoint into their application.

302.description: Redirect to FRONTEND_URL/calendar with a status query param

get.description: Use this endpoint to verify if the application is connected to your Google Calendar account and whether any data synchronization is in progress.

delete.description: Removes all Google Calendar integration, including push notifications and tokens. Requires authentication.

post.description: This endpoint allows you to manually sync upcoming events from your Google Calendar into meetings. It requires a valid Bearer token for authentication.
This endpoint is triggered by Google to acknowledge push notifications for Google Calendar. It does not require authentication and responds with 200 immediately without any payload.

get.description: This endpoint lists up to 7 days worth of scheduled meetings. Developers can use this to integrate real-time meeting updates into their applications.

post.description: Use this endpoint to create a meeting that also automatically adds a corresponding event to the user's Google Calendar, providing a unique Meet link for the session.

delete.description: This API endpoint allows users to cancel a meeting by specifying the meeting's unique ID. It requires the user to be authorized and only allows the meeting creator or an admin to perform this action, soft-deleting the meeting by setting its status to 'cancelled'.

post.description: This API endpoint handles standup commands in Discord, verifying the request signature for security. It requires a valid JSON payload with a Discord interaction payload, and returns an acknowledgment or response based on the command executed.

200.description: Interaction response (PING ack or slash-command reply)

post.description: This endpoint allows the submission of standup records for a specific Discord user. It requires the use of a shared internal token for authentication and expects the inclusion of the user's Discord name, the previous day's status, the current day's status, and any blockers encountered.

get.description: This API allows you to retrieve the SMTP settings for a specific employee by providing their unique ID. Useful for applications that need to access email configuration details for different users.

put.summary: Update SMTP settings for an employee
put.description: This API allows updating the SMTP settings for a specific employee. It requires the employeeId in the path and the SMTP settings in the request body. The API checks for required fields and handles password updates according to the specification.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves an array of stored service credentials associated with a specific employee, ensuring secure password handling as no actual passwords are returned.

post.summary: Create or update employee service credentials
post.description: This endpoint allows you to create or update a service credential for an employee. The employee's ID is specified in the path, and the service name and password are provided in the request body. If no service name is provided, a 400 error is returned.

get.description: This endpoint is used to verify a webhook challenge and mode sent by the service provider. It echoes back the hub.challenge if the verify_token matches the expected value for the service, ensuring the connection is secure and functional.

200.description: Challenge echoed back as plain text

post.description: This endpoint receives a payload from an external service and always responds with a 200 status to acknowledge receipt, even handling Slack-style POST verification for authentication purposes.

schema.description: Arbitrary event payload, or a Slack url_verification challenge

200.description: Acknowledged (or challenge echoed for Slack verification)

get.description: This endpoint allows your application to trigger a month-end report generation through an n8n workflow. It returns a success message or indicates errors in communication with the n8n workflow.

200.description: sucessfully send data to n8n webhook

503.description: Error in sending request to n8n workflow

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Which onboarding form layout to fetch

get.description: This API endpoint allows you to fetch the onboarding form layout for either 'intern' or 'employee' types. You can specify the type in the query parameter to get the corresponding form layout.

post.description: Changes the layout of onboarding forms. Requires admin or lead permissions to execute.

get.description: This endpoint allows you to retrieve an array of onboarding profiles, specifying the type (all, intern, employee) you are interested in. Use this to filter and access different types of onboarding profiles.

post.description: This endpoint allows users to submit their onboarding application with a signed contract. The request includes a JSON payload and the signed contract as a binary file in the request body.

patch.description: This API allows approvers to approve an onboarding profile. It requires the user to have the appropriate permissions and is only accessible via a PATCH request with a specified profile ID in the path.

delete.description: This API endpoint allows administrators to delete a specific onboarding profile by its ID, requiring administrative privileges.

get.description: This endpoint allows you to download the contract file associated with a specific onboarding profile by its ID. You need to provide the profile ID in the request URL to access the contract file securely.
